bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM inspects 'Nitish Setu' bridge ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's November visit
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM inspects 'Nitish Setu' bridge ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's November visit ANI | Updated: Nov 18, 2026 16:40 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [ India ], November 18 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary inspected the newly completed Kacchi Dargah–Bidupur Six-Lane Bridge on Sunday, setting the stage for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's upcoming visit to inaugurate the infrastructure corridor and launch multiple development initiatives across the state. Highlighting the project's origins, the Chief Minister credited Kumar's long-term administrative vision for steering the initiative since its inception. "Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the sacred land of Bihar on the 21st to inaugurate the "Nitish Setu" (bridge) and dedicate it to the public. In addition to this, he will also perform the inauguration and foundation-stone-laying ceremonies for several other projects across various departments. The realisation of this entire bridge project is the result of the vision, understanding, and persistent efforts of Nitish Kumar ji, an initiative that began back in 2012," Choudhary told reporters Bihar CM further noted that naming the bridge after the senior leader serves as a tribute to two decades of public service, fulfilling a commitment originally made to local residents ahead of the 2010 elections. He said, "This follows a commitment Nitish Kumar ji made to the local people during a public meeting here ahead of the 2010 elections, a promise to construct a bridge in this area. We are, therefore, proud and delighted to have named this bridge after Nitish Kumar ji. It is a modest gesture on our part to honour the 20 years of dedicated service he has rendered to Bihar ." During his upcoming visit, Prime Minister Modi will formally open the six-lane corridor and lay foundation stones for a series of multi-sector development projects across the state. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Bihar on November 21 and reach Vaishali, where he will inaugurate the Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane bridge and inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for several development projects in the state. The details of the Prime Minister's visit were shared during a press conference addressed by the state presidents of NDA constituents. BJP Bihar president Sanjay Saraogi said the NDA government would complete one year in office on November 20 and a major programme would be organised at Raja Pakar block to mark the occasion. He said Modi would visit Bihar on November 21 to participate in the programme and described the Prime Minister's visits to the state as occasions when Bihar receives several development projects. "Whenever the Prime Minister visits Bihar , he gives several gifts to the state. His dedication towards Bihar and his resolve to build a developed Bihar have been consistently visible," Saraogi said. Preparations are underway to make the Prime Minister's visit to Vaishali a historic and memorable event. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Museum and the Case for Investing in Heritage - Frontline
bihar_raw_news.content: DIGITAL EXCLUSIVE The Bihar Museum and using heritage as a calling card The museum, which has made it to the global top ten, shows how heritage can become a strategic asset when sustained public, private, and citizens’ investments create quality institutions that draw visitors and break the cycle of low footfall. Published : Nov 18, 2026 16:17 IST - 7 MINS READ Anu Singh Lather, Tarun Agarwal AI Summary COMMents SHARE Copy link Email Facebook Twitter Telegram LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit READ LATER SEE ALL Remove Artefacts on display inside the Bihar Museum in Patna on October 30, 2026. | Photo Credit: PTI Ask most Indians what a museum means to them, and the answer is usually a memory from school: a bus ride, a dimly lit gallery, a worksheet, and a teacher counting heads at the exit. Few would have predicted that the next time an Indian museum makes international headlines, it would be for outranking the Louvre. In late October, Worth a Journey , the Munich-based travel guide, placed the Bihar Museum in Patna ninth on its list of the world’s 100 best museums for 2026, ahead of New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art (10th) and the Louvre (31st). It is the highest-ranked museum in Asia and the only Indian entry. Such rankings reflect visitor reviews, data analytics, and on-site expert assessments rather than the depth or scholarly significance of collections, and should be read with that caution. The result, nonetheless, shows what becomes possible when heritage is treated as a serious public investment and sustained over a decade. With the next Union Budget approaching, two questions follow. Why should a developing country, with many legitimate claims on its resources, invest more in its museums? And how should that investment be financed so that it endures? We argue that heritage is a strategic asset, and that its future depends on sustained public investment complemented by a wider partnership between the state, citizens, and private institutions. The strategic case begins with attraction. Political scientist Joseph Nye defined soft power as the ability to obtain preferred outcomes through attraction rather than coercion or payment. India’s civilisational inheritance is among its strongest sources of attraction, but a narrative persuades most when people can see it, walk through it, and remember it. Museums give that narrative a physical address. Shared heritage is also a resource for diplomacy. The heritage scholar Tim Winter describes heritage diplomacy as the process through which pasts shared across nations become the basis for exchange and cooperation. India’s Buddhist heritage, much of it rooted in Bihar, links it to societies across South, Southeast, and East Asia, and the Bihar Museum’s 2025 Biennale, “Global South: Sharing Histories”, brought institutions from Asia, Africa, and Latin America to Patna. Such diplomacy is also competitive. Winter has shown how China has framed its Belt and Road Initiative through a curated history of the Silk Roads, presenting itself as the principal narrator of Eurasia’s shared past. bihar_raw_news.title: SMAT 2026: Bihar pull off last-over win as Chhattisgarh defeat Odisha
bihar_raw_news.content: SMAT 2026: Bihar pull off last-over win as Chhattisgarh defeat Odisha Bihar edged Delhi by two wickets in a thrilling chase in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Elite 2026. Chhattisgarh, Andhra and Bengal also registered victories, with Vikalp Tiwari's century and several impressive batting performances highlighting Wednesday's matches By IANS Published Date - 18 November 2026, 02:18 PM Smat 2026 New Delhi: Bihar pulled off a thrilling two-wicket victory over Delhi, chasing down a target of 225 with one ball to spare, as the first four matches of the day in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) Elite 2026 produced plenty of runs and several standout individual performances on Wednesday. At the Daly College Ground in Indore, Delhi rode on a sensational 125 off 59 balls from Yash Dhull and a quickfire 51 off 25 deliveries by Tejasvi Dahiya to post 224/5 in 20 overs. Dhull struck 16 fours and seven sixes, while Dahiya contributed four boundaries and four sixes. However, Bihar responded with an aggressive start. Ayush Loharuka smashed 50 off just 22 balls, while Bipin Saurabh made 49 off 19, putting the chase firmly on course. Raghuvendra Pratap Singh added 25 off 15 balls and later finished as Bihar’s leading bowler with figures of 3/44. Despite a late wobble, Bihar reached 227/8 in 19.5 overs to secure the win, with Raghuvendra named Player of the Match. At the Jadavpur University Campus Ground in Kolkata, Chhattisgarh defeated Odisha by 51 runs after captain Vikalp Tiwari produced a magnificent century. Tiwari struck 119 off 56 balls, reaching his hundred in just 44 deliveries, while Ajay Jadav Mandal chipped in with 50 off 28 balls as Chhattisgarh posted 228/4. Odisha managed 177/8 in reply, with Kartik Biswal top-scoring with 57 off 33 balls. Subhranshu Senapati added 31, but Chhattisgarh’s bowlers kept the chase under control, with Jayant Yadav, Dev Aditya Singh and Sourabh Majumdar picking up two or more wickets each. Andhra registered a 29-run win over Kerala at the Punjab Cricket Association IS Bindra Stadium in Mohali. Seeram Venkata Rahul led the batting effort with 64 off 30 balls, while Shaik Rasheed scored 60 off 39. Contributions from Maramreddy Hemanth Reddy (32 off 16) and Ashwin Hebbar (37 off 15) powered Andhra to 225/7. Kerala fought back through Abdul Basith’s 70 off 35 balls, supported by Govind Dev Pai (36) and Sanju Samson (26), but finished at 196/5. MD Nidheesh claimed three wickets for Kerala, while Andhra’s KV Sasikanth and K S Narasimha Raju took two wickets apiece. Bengal completed a seven-wicket victory over Jharkhand at the Sharad Pawar Cricket Academy in Mumbai. After restricting Jharkhand to 148/7, Bengal chased down the target in 18.4 overs, finishing at 149/3. Abhimanyu Easwaran remained unbeaten on 61 off 48 balls, while Abishek Porel contributed 49 off 34. Jharkhand’s innings was built around Virat Singh’s unbeaten 45 and Shikhar Mohan’s 42, but Bengal’s bowlers ensured the total remained within reach. bihar_raw_news.title: NITI Aayog Begins National Workshop Series to Highlight 25 Years of PM Modi's Leadership
bihar_raw_news.content: Home · News NITI Aayog today launched the first workshop of its five-part national workshop series, titled ‘Leadership as Mission’, at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The series aims to draw lessons from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 25 years as Head of Government and will continue until October next year. The remaining four workshops will focus on Governance as Delivery, Development as Inclusion, Civilisational Identity and India’s Global Role. The first workshop featured first-hand accounts of key governance initiatives, including the reconstruction of Kutch following the 2001 earthquake, India’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Lakhpati Didi initiative and the opening up of the space sector. Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister Dr P. K. Mishra and NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri attended the workshop. Viksit Bharat 2047 Requires Sustained Economic Growth Addressing the gathering, NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri said that Viksit Bharat 2047 represents a systematic, target-driven approach to economic transformation. He stated that India aims to become a USD 30–40 trillion economy by the centenary of its independence in 2047. He underlined that achieving this target would require a sustained annual real GDP growth rate of 7–10 per cent. Lahiri also highlighted the vision of building advanced digital public infrastructure that goes beyond basic financial inclusion to support livelihoods, productivity, decentralised credit access, AI integration and the expansion of MSME markets. He added that the vision includes achieving 100 per cent literacy, net-zero carbon emissions, and a life expectancy of more than 80 years, with a focus on youth, the poor, women, and farmers. PM Modi’s Leadership Based on Integrity, Teamwork and Technology In his address, Dr P K Mishra highlighted three key principles that have shaped Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership over the past 25 years: integrity, teamwork and technology. He said the workshop would benefit people from diverse backgrounds, including government officers involved in nation-building over the next two decades, youth, students and community members. Emphasising the difference between a mission and a programme, Dr Mishra said a mission involves clear goals, defined timelines, public participation and accountability at every level. He noted that this approach helps transform government initiatives into people’s movements. He also said that 25 years of governance under Prime Minister Modi, first as Chief Minister of Gujarat and later as Prime Minister, offer valuable lessons from large-scale public initiatives. Dr Mishra highlighted that the success of these initiatives reflects the collective efforts of government officials, professionals, frontline workers and citizens. Their experiences, he said, serve as a valuable national asset for shaping India’s future governance. He further explained that the Prime Minister’s leadership philosophy emphasises a clear vision, the courage to execute it, empathy, and inclusion to ensure that development reaches every citizen. national_raw_news.title: Improved infrastructure and business environment make India attractive destination for Japanese ...
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has called for strengthening India-Japan cooperation in key areas, including economic security, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, critical minerals, clean energy and defence. Addressing the inaugural event of Raisina Tokyo 2026, Dr Jaishankar said the rapidly changing global landscape has made trusted partnerships, supply chain diversification and stronger national capacities increasingly important. Dr Jaishankar said India and Japan, as leading nations of the Indo-Pacific committed to a free and open region, must deepen reliable cooperation while safeguarding their national interests and promoting regional stability. Mr Jaishankar said the transformation of India, particularly since 2014, has improved the country’s infrastructure, business environment and manufacturing potential, making it an increasingly attractive destination for Japanese investment and production. He also highlighted India’s progress in education, skill development, innovation and start-ups, citing opportunities for cooperation in digital technology, space, drones, healthcare and defence. The Minister identified artificial intelligence, pharmaceuticals, information and communication technology and clean energy among the areas offering greater scope for bilateral collaboration. Calling for stronger people-to-people ties, he stressed the need to expand exchanges in education, culture and language. Dr Jaishankar outlined five defining features of the current global landscape- repeated shocks to the international system, weaponisation and strategic chokepoints, extreme competition and greater risk-taking, de-risking and diversification, and the growing importance of trusted partnerships. Dr Jaishankar said India and Japan are members of the Quad, partners in the G4 initiative for United Nations reform and participants in the East Asia Summit. He said stronger India-Japan ties would contribute to stability and security in the Indo-Pacific and strengthen the foundations of a multipolar Asia and a multipolar world.

national_raw_news.title: Women’s Asian Champions hockey tournament begins tomorrow in Bhopal: 6 teams, including India in fray 4 hours ago 82
national_raw_news.content: The Women’s Asian Champions Trophy 2026 hockey tournament will begin in Bhopal tomorrow. The tournament will continue till 28th of this month. Apart from India, teams from China, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia and Thailand will participate in the tournament. India has won this title three times in 2016, 2023 and 2024. India will begin its campaign against Malaysia tomorrow. The match will start at 7 PM. Recently, the Indian women’s hockey team defeated China to win the gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games after 44 years. With this victory, the team also qualified for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The Asian Champions Trophy will be country’s first international tournament after its Asian Games victory. All six teams will play against each other in the league stage. Each team will play five matches, and the top four teams in the points table will qualify for the semi-finals. League matches will be held from 19th to 25th September. Both semi-finals and the match for fifth place will take place on 27th of this month. The bronze medal match and the final will be played on 28th of this month. India will face South Korea on 21st November, Thailand on 22nd, and China on 24th November. The Indian team will play its final league match against Japan on 25th November.

He encouraged them to uphold the ideals of compassion, humanity and selfless service inspired by Lord Mahavira. national_raw_news.title: Elections 73 Uttar Pradesh publishes draft electoral roll for 2027 Assembly polls with 13.58 crore voters
national_raw_news.content: Uttar Pradesh’s draft electoral roll for the 2027 Assembly elections has been published. It comprises 13.58 crore voters after a net addition of 18.84 lakh electorates during the Special Summary Revision (SSR). UP Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Navdeep Rinwa said, the draft roll updates the previous final list released on April 10, 2026, after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Out of a total of 13.58 crore voters, Men account for 7.38 crore, while Women account for 6.20 crore, reflecting an addition of nearly 11 lakh female electors since the April 2026 roll. The roll includes 4,042 third-gender electors. Citizens in the 18-19 age group represent 11.83 lakh of the total voters. The revision is being conducted with January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date for eligible citizens turning 18. Eligible residents can file their claims and objections from November 17 to December 16, 2026. Citizens can use Form 6 for new voter inclusion, Form 7 for deletion of names, and Form 8 for correcting existing entries. Election officials will resolve all submitted claims and objections by December 28, 2026. The final electoral roll will be published on January 4, 2027. Voters can inspect the roll at all 1,73,730 polling booths across the state’s 403 Assembly constituencies in 75 districts, or check their status online via the CEO Uttar Pradesh Portal.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi returns to New Delhi after a successful two-day visit to Philippines
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi returned to New Delhi after successfully concluding his two-day visit to Manila, the Philippines. During the visit, Mr Modi participated in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit, the 21st East Asia Summit and the Quad Leaders’ Meeting. Prime Minister also visited the historic Gurudwara Khalsa Diwan in Manila and took part in the ceremony marking the commencement of its redevelopment. Mr Modi also met Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., and the two leaders discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in defence, security, trade and investment. The prime minister also discussed regional and global issues of mutual interest with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand on the sidelines of the visit. At the annual ASEAN-India summit, the prime minister proposed nine initiatives, including a long-term maritime plan to boost connectivity and ensure seafarers’ security, free e-visas for tourists from the bloc’s member nations, cooperation on mining and critical minerals, and a framework for technical exchanges in the civil nuclear energy sector. In his remarks, Modi underlined the importance New Delhi attaches to its comprehensive strategic partnership with ASEAN and affirmed the two sides should work for peace, stability and predictability in the region and beyond. At the Quad Summit, Mr Modi said for India, the Quad is a “constructive and trusted” partnership that strives to deliver trusted solutions across the Indo-Pacific, spanning maritime security, supply chains, new technologies, and disaster response. The Quad is a strategic grouping of India, the US, Japan and Australia that works to promote a free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific through cooperation on maritime security, technology, infrastructure and regional stability. During his address at the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS), Mr Modi announced the launch of a seafarers’ safety initiative to boost joint training and emergency response among EAS nations, emphasising that safeguarding maritime security and freedom of navigation is essential to protecting the seas as a lifeline of shared prosperity. ASEAN is a regional grouping comprising 11 Southeast Asian countries — Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia and Timor-Leste. India, along with the US, China, Japan and Australia, is among its dialogue partners.

national_raw_news.content: The Quad leaders have announced a series of initiatives to strengthen maritime security, artificial intelligence cooperation, cybersecurity and critical infrastructure connectivity across the Indo-Pacific at the Manila Summit in the Philippines. The summit brought together Prime Minister Narendra Modi, US President Donald Trump, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. In a joint press release, the four leaders reaffirmed their commitment to a free, open, safe and prosperous Indo-Pacific, describing the Quad as a “partnership of action” dedicated to peace, stability and prosperity. The meeting also marked nearly a decade since the revival of the Quad and the 10th anniversary of the vision of a Free and Open Indo-Pacific, first articulated by the late Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe in 2016. The leaders strongly opposed destabilising or unilateral actions aimed at changing the status quo through force or coercion, saying such actions escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability. They also expressed grave concern over economic coercion, including arbitrary export restrictions. Emphasising the importance of resilient supply chains, freedom of navigation and overflight, and the use of emerging technologies, the leaders committed to working together to ensure open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors across the Indo-Pacific. The four countries announced the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum, scheduled to be held in early 2027. The forum will bring together business leaders, government officials and policy experts from the four countries to strengthen private-sector engagement, promote commercial deals and develop partnerships that contribute to the prosperity of the Indo-Pacific.

national_raw_news.title: Northern Railway facilitates travel of 1.82 crore passengers during festive season 2 hours ago 25
national_raw_news.content: Northern Railway has successfully facilitated the travel of nearly 1.82 crore passengers during Puja and the festive season this year. It registered an increase of around 10 lakh passengers compared to the corresponding period last year. Through strategic capacity enhancement, an expanded fleet of special trains, coach augmentations, and continuous demand monitoring, the zone significantly outperformed its previous year’s operational benchmarks. According to the Northern Railway, seven thousand 85 special train trips were operated during the festive season of Diwali and Chhath Puja, compared to four thousand 666 trips last year. This means around 54 additional special train trips were operated every day to manage the festive rush. Daily passenger handling also increased from approximately 3 lakh 91 thousand to 4 lakh 14 thousand, accommodating nearly 22 thousand 700 additional passengers every day. Of the total passengers carried, around 1 crore 66 lakh travelled through regular train services, while 12 lakh 83 thousand were accommodated through special Trains on Demand services. To maximise capacity on high-demand routes, Northern Railway added 581 coaches to regular trains this year, while 123 coaches were added during the corresponding period last year, which shows an increase of approximately 372 percent this time around. By combining proactive fleet expansion with real-time crowd and demand monitoring, Northern Railway ensured reliable connectivity and enhanced comfort for millions of festive travellers across its network.

national_raw_news.content: New Delhi: 3rd DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit brings together over 600 scientists, researchers, policymakers Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर New Delhi: 3rd DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit brings together over 600 scientists, researchers, policymakers ANI | Updated: Nov 18, 2026 14:28 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 18 (ANI): The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has achieved the milestone of 100 successful technology transfer deals, marking a significant step in translating indigenous health research into technologies and solutions for wider public use. The milestone was announced at the 3rd Department of Health Research (DHR)-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit, which concluded today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Organised by DHR and ICMR on 16 and 17 November 2026, the two-day Summit brought together over 600 scientists, researchers, innovators, administrators and policymakers from ICMR institutes, partner institutions, government organisations and academia. The Summit also marked 115 years of ICMR's contribution to biomedical and health research in the country, according to a press release issued by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The Summit serves as a national platform for recognising excellence in health research and promoting the translation of scientific evidence into tangible outcomes. It showcases significant contributions from ICMR institutes and extramural partner institutions across research publications, technologies, patents and research management, while facilitating collaboration among researchers, industry and policymakers. At the Technology Transfer Ceremony, ICMR exchanged 20 licensing agreements covering eight technologies with nine Indian companies, taking the cumulative number of successful technology transfer deals to 100 within a limited time of less than 2 years of Medical Innovations Patent Mitra, a flagship initiative of ICMR launched by Union Health and Family Welfare Minister, Shri J P Nadda, in March 2025. This milestone reflects ICMR's continued efforts to facilitate the translation of research and indigenous innovations into practical applications through industry partnerships. As per the release, an Innovation Exhibition showcased 17 technologies developed by ICMR institutes and extramural partner institutions. In addition, 10 technologies and eight patents were presented during a dedicated session on Technologies and Patents, highlighting the breadth of innovation emerging from the country's health research ecosystem. Three new initiatives were launched at the Summit. The DHR’s new Research to Action Vertical will translate research evidence into decision-ready products for policy and programmes. Syndromic Surveillance under the DHR Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDL) Scheme will create an early-warning network for outbreaks across 70 VRDLs and Infectious Disease Research & Diagnostic Laboratories (IRDLs). The Dr M K Bhan Young Medical Faculty PhD Portal launched today will serve as a centralised digital platform with information for prospective applicants, the release said. ICMR also released the Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Annual Report and Standard Operating Procedures, bringing together the national evidence base on antimicrobial resistance and standardised laboratory procedures. The ICMR Compendium, featuring 25 stories of research translated into outcomes for people, was also released. national_raw_news.content: Union Sports Minister Mandaviya calls for integrated national sports ecosystem built around universities Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Sports Minister Mandaviya calls for integrated national sports ecosystem built around universities ANI | Updated: Nov 18, 2026 14:19 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 18 (ANI): Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya, chaired a meeting with 13 Sports Universities from across India, in New Delhi on Wednesday. The discussions revolved around strengthening collaboration among Sports Universities, sharing expertise and resources, and building an integrated ecosystem to enhance India’s sports education, research, training, and global competitiveness, as per a press release from the Union Youth Affairs and Sports Ministry. Dr Mandaviya said, “Our vision is to make Sports Universities the hub of the entire sports ecosystem, where athletes, coaches, training, research, competitions, and world-class infrastructure are all developed together.” The Union Sports Minister encouraged all universities to develop their own expertise in particular sports to benefit the country. “Every university needs to develop its own specific expertise – whether in a particular sport, coaching, sports science, or research. This will benefit the entire nation,” he said. While the Minister envisioned that the universities develop their own niche areas of expertise, he also encouraged them to partake in knowledge-sharing with each other. “We will no longer work in silos. By integrating our efforts, resources, and expertise, we will build a strong, collaborative national sports ecosystem,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “Every Coach exchange, knowledge exchange, and resource sharing among universities will be promoted. Despite the fact that a major part of the focus remains on furthering the capabilities of India’s athletes, Dr. Mandaviya also encouraged the universities to build systems that would help India grow its sporting ecosystem and industry as a whole. “Universities must focus on developing specialised expertise in emerging sectors such as Sports Science, Sports Law, and Sports Tourism, to develop skilled professionals and strong institutional capabilities in these fields across India,” said Dr Mandaviya. “Sports Universities must not limit themselves to just athletes, but also develop sports professionals who can contribute to sports management, administration, and the overall sports ecosystem,” he further stated. “Our goal is for Indian Sports Universities to make their mark at the global level and establish their place among the world's leading universities.” The meeting was attended by Hon’ble Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports, Raksha Khadse, Secretary (Sports) Hari Ranjan Rao, and Vice-Chancellors and other representatives from 13 Sports Universities across the country. national_raw_news.title: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra finds place in 'Third 100 IUGS Geological Heritage Sites'
national_raw_news.content: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra finds place in 'Third 100 IUGS Geological Heritage Sites' | Mathrubhumi English Home page » Technology » Science » Geological Heritage Lonar Lake in Maharashtra finds place in 'Third 100 IUGS Geological Heritage Sites' # PTI Last Updated: 18 November 2026, 02:47 PM IST Follow us on Nagpur: Lonar Lake, a meteorite-impact crater located in the Buldhana district of Maharashtra, has been included in the prestigious list of the 'Third 100 IUGS Geological Heritage Sites'. The International Union of Geological Sciences (IUGS) recognises Geological Heritage Sites for their outstanding scientific value as exceptional examples of geological features, processes, and discoveries, a release issued by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) said. They represent some of the world's most significant places for understanding the Earth and its history. Located across the globe, they offer a surprising journey through the most important geological sites of the Earth. The release said the selection of the 'Third 100' builds on the success and global impact of the 'First 100', announced in Zumaia, Spain, in 2022, and the 'Second 100', announced during the 37th International Geological Congress (IGC 2024) in Busan, Republic of Korea. Since 2022, more than 1,000 experts from 90 countries and 20 international organisations have contributed to this programme by proposing sites, participating in the selection process, and evaluating their scientific quality. With 74 active national members, IUGS is one of the world's largest scientific organisations. It encourages international cooperation and participation in the Earth sciences in relation to human welfare. Lonar Lake crater in Buldhana is one of the youngest (approximately 12,000 years old) and best-preserved bowl-shaped hypervelocity impact structures on Earth. With a diameter of approximately 1.88 km, it is uniquely situated within the extensive Deccan Traps, a succession of tholeiitic continental flood basalts formed around 65 million years ago, according to the release. It is particularly significant as one of the rare terrestrial impact craters formed in basaltic rocks and is considered one of the five known hypervelocity meteorite impact craters on Earth developed in a basaltic target. The crater hosts a saline-alkaline lake at its centre, creating a distinctive geological and ecological setting. Its circular morphology, depth-to-diameter ratio, exposed basaltic lava flows along the inner slopes, brecciated subsurface rocks, outward-dipping country rocks, debris mounds, and extensive ejecta deposits containing fragmented breccia and suevite provide compelling evidence of its meteoritic impact origin, it said.
